Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows near-complete opacification of the right hemithorax with a contralateral (leftward) mediastinal shift, which is characteristic of a large pleural effusion pushing structures away; thoracentesis is the appropriate next step for diagnosis and symptom relief. In contrast, lung collapse would typically cause an ipsilateral shift, and pneumothorax would appear radiolucent rather than opaque.
